name: centrifugal_compressor_lookup_map
title: Centrifugal compressor with a lookup-table performance map (air)
summary: Constant-speed centrifugal air compressor characterised by a three-point performance map: reduced mass flow rate and isentropic efficiency interpolated from the map at the pressure ratio, then mass flow rate and absorbed power. Native EES INTERPOLATE form (blocked); a runnable variant ships beside it.
language_features: INTERPOLATE (native EES call form with a named argument)

authors: TBD (ULiège MSTh course — Machines et systèmes thermiques; course team J. Lebrun, V. Lemort, S. Bertagnolio; individual author not identified)
origin.course: ULiège, Machines et systèmes thermiques, repetition 4 (2004-10-12), exercise 6

verification.reference: EES stored solution of thermo_models TM-0061 (EES 7.210, 12 variables, internally consistent run at p_ex = 5.4 bar / r_p = 6.0), compared with tools/compare_solution.py (variant)
verification.notes: Concerns the runnable variant. p_su, p_ex, r_p, t_su exact; w_s 9.55e-04 (largest comparable deviation; EES 7 vs CoolProp Air, within the 0.5 % tolerance); h_su, h_exs and s_su are left out of the comparison (constant EES-7-vs-CoolProp Air reference-state offsets: +125.87 kJ/kg on h, -1814.8 J/kg-K on s). epsilon_s, M_r, M_dot and W_dot differ at r_p = 6 only because EES extrapolates the map linearly where CoolSolve clamps (CS-GAP-INTERP-EXTRAP): applying the extrapolation by hand reproduces all four stored values (epsilon_s 1.093333, M_r 29.9, M_dot 1.572099 rel 1e-10, W_dot 283013 with the CoolSolve w_s, rel 9.6e-4 = the w_s deviation; 282742.25 exactly with the EES w_s). The 127x2 parametric table of the original is not usable as reference (lost .lkt, values inconsistent with the published map - see README).

related_external: CoolSolve examples/turbocompressor_interpolate.eescode (CSX-045: same exercise, kept in CoolSolve as a test case; p_ex imposed at 4.5 bar and map data only in comments, see README)
